sources.title: Google Books metadata and preview page for Measure What Matters
sources.role: primary edition metadata, official preview framing, and partial contents map
sources.notes: Confirms John Doerr as author, Penguin publication on 2018-04-24, 320 pages, ISBN 9780525536239, and a visible contents listing spanning the OKR, CFR, culture, and future-goals sections.

sources.title: Open Library 2018 Portfolio edition record for Measure What Matters
sources.notes: Confirms the 2018 Portfolio edition family and the April 24, 2018 publication date.

sources.title: Open Library work page for Measure What Matters
sources.role: work-level metadata and dust-jacket summary support
sources.notes: Confirms the 2018 hardcover family, 320 pages, Larry Page foreword, and the dust-jacket summary covering Google, Intel, transparency, and the benefits of OKRs.

sources.title: What Matters explainer on John Doerr's Operation Crush story
sources.role: authorized support for the Intel-origin material and Chapter 3 anchor set
sources.notes: Provides authorized summary support for Andy Grove, Operation Crush, Intel's crisis response, bottom-up feedback, and the role of OKRs in the microprocessor battle.

sources.title: What Matters OKRs Explained course index
sources.role: authorized support for the OKR fundamentals and the book's superpower framing
sources.notes: Confirms the active What Matters learning path, the Five Benefits of OKRs framing, and the continuity between the book and John Doerr's public OKR teaching.

sources.title: What Matters The OKR Origin Story
sources.role: authorized support for Andy Grove as the father of OKRs and for the execution-first origin logic
sources.notes: Supports Grove as the father of OKRs, frames the method as a response to expertise without execution, and links Doerr to Grove's teaching.

sources.title: What Matters What are OKRs? Explanation and Examples
sources.role: authorized support for OKR definition, transparency, and Doerr as the Johnny Appleseed of OKRs
sources.notes: Confirms that Andy Grove created the method at Intel, taught it to John Doerr, and that OKRs are used to maximize alignment and transparency.

sources.title: What Matters stretch goals and the Five Benefits of OKRs
sources.role: authorized support for the FACTS framing, especially focus and commitment
sources.notes: Supports the Five Benefits of OKRs and defines focus as choosing what matters most and commitment as participation and buy-in from stakeholders.

sources.title: Measure What Matters notes by Gustavo Millen
sources.role: chapter-level interpretive support for early OKR chapters
sources.notes: Supports the early-book chapter map and highlights for the Google opening, Andy Grove, and OKR operating rules.

sources.title: Codurance book-club writeup of Measure What Matters
sources.role: support for later CFR and culture chapters when public preview text is thin
sources.notes: Provides chapter-level support around continuous performance management, CFRs, and the cultural implications of OKRs.
